title: The Simple Past
label: ch:ge-praeteritum
canDo: I can recognise the one-word past German uses in writing, produce the handful of its forms that people actually say out loud, and explain why the rest of it retreated.

payoff.summary: German's second past means exactly what the first one means, so this chapter separates the two by register rather than by tense: produce the Perfekt, recognise the Präteritum, and learn the short list of forms that ignore the rule. It ends with the reason the tense retreated at all — the same change ran through French and Italian over the same centuries, because their speakers are neighbours.
payoff.note: Chapter 17 is generated from schema-v2 lessons, so the payoff is atom-scored. It claims every atom the chapter introduces; the Präteritum-against-Perfekt table in the practice lesson pairs forms that have each had a lesson, and its first column is a meaning rather than a person, so it is a comparison rather than a paradigm.
